Hi Maya / Monica —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our engineering lead asked me to lock down the model choices and the conversation window so we can finalize infra and procurement. A few quick data points attached (conversant_prod_metrics_q4.xlsx):
- Expected concurrent active users at launch: 250–400 during peak US hours
- Avg messages per user per session: 4 (1.2k messages/minute peak)
- Typical prompt + assistant length today ~ 600 tokens (including metadata).

Initial asks:
1) Recommended model shortlist (we prefer open-weight options; latency < 400ms median if possible).
2) Suggestion on context window tradeoffs — we are debating 8k vs 32k.
3) A rough hourly token projection for the first 90 days (peaks vs baseline).

Can you send a short plan/attachment we can share with our infra and procurement teams? Would like to lock decisions by Monday (the 21st) so procurement can kick off.

Thanks — happy to sync if you want to run numbers together.

— Alice

Alice —

Appreciate the metrics. I sketched a concise plan below so your procurement and infra teams have concrete inputs. I also attached a one-page MAP (MAP_v1.xlsx) that lists owners and deadlines. High-level recommendations:

Model shortlist (prioritized):
- Falcon-40B-chat (8k) — best latency/cost balance for your traffic profile
- Redstone-34B-extended (32k option) — candidate if you decide long-term context is critical
- Llama2-13B-QLoRA (quantized) — lower-cost fallback for bursty traffic and smaller queries

Context window guidance:
- Start with 8k: preserves latency and keeps GPU memory requirements modest. Based on your avg 600-token exchanges, 8k covers ~12 turns and most session histories.
- Run an A/B for a subset (5–10%) on 32k for use cases that need long context (threaded support tickets).

Token projection (90d) — conservative baseline vs peak:
- Baseline: 40k tokens/hour (off-peak)
- Peak initial (US evening): 160k tokens/hour
- Anticipated steady-state after month 3: 240k tokens/hour (with adoption growth)

Operational notes:
- Cacheable prefixes: 35–45% of tokens look like repeated system/context; enabling prefix caching will materially cut effective token cost.
- Batch sizing: use dynamic batching for short requests, fixed windows for long-context inference to keep 95th p99 latency < 500ms.
- Canary plan: start hosted API with 20% traffic to the Redstone 32k variant once we validate latency on pilot data.

Deliverables I’ll produce Monday AM: short technical sizing (token_profile_conversant.csv), estimated cost delta 8k vs 32k, and a suggested rollout MAP.

If procurement needs a cost figure for an initial reserved pool, cc Ben and we’ll provide a ballpark.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick: model shortlist & context window for production pilot

Thanks Maya — attaching token_profile_conversant.csv with hourly slices and a 7-day sample projection. Key technical notes (summary):

1) Memory and GPU footprint
- Falcon-40B-chat (8k): ~48GB per replica with int8 quantization; supports ~150–200k tokens/hour on a modest pool with continuous batching.
- Redstone-34B-extended (32k): ~140GB memory footprint in 16k KV splits; higher per-replica cost and limits autoscaling granularity.
- Llama2-13B-QLoRA: sweet spot for cost reduction during off-peak/fallback.

2) Context tradeoffs
- 8k: keeps latency predictable and makes autoscaling reactive. Good first milestone.
- 32k: only enable for specific routes where long thread state materially improves accuracy. Estimate +2.5–3.8x cost on tokens served if all traffic migrated to 32k.

3) Caching & batching impact
- We measured that enabling prefix/KV caching reduces token compute by ~27% for typical support flows.
- Recommend a cache TTL of 20 minutes for session-level context.

4) Recommended initial capacity (pilot week)
- Hosted: 4 medium replicas of Falcon-40B-chat (8k) with autoscale to 8 replicas for peak.
- Dedicated (if procurement prefers reserved): 2x 48GB GPU nodes reserved + 2 burst nodes.

Attachments: token_profile_conversant.csv (hourly token bands), quick_cost_delta_8k_vs_32k.xlsx (summary table).

I can run a quick sim with your sample logs if you share 48 hours of representative traffic — will tighten the hourly projections.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
